record.paper_title: Feynman integrals as generalized functions on path space: things done and open problems
record.original_question: Within the white-noise generalized-function approach to Feynman path integrals, can the construction of non-perturbative Feynman integrals be extended by weakening the requirement that the expression inside the relevant expectation be integrable, while still yielding a valid T-transform and hence a well-defined generalized white-noise functional?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and setup. Let $(\mathcal{S}'(\mathbb{R}), \mathcal{B}, \mu)$ be the white noise probability space, where $\mu$ is the standard Gaussian (white noise) measure on the space $\mathcal{S}'(\mathbb{R})$ of tempered distributions. Let $(\mathcal{S}) \subset L^2(\mu) \subset (\mathcal{S})^*$ be the Hida triple of test and generalized white noise functionals. For $\Phi \in (\mathcal{S})^*$, the T-transform is defined by
$$ (T\Phi)(\xi) \;=\; \langle\!\langle \Phi,\; \exp(i\langle \cdot,\xi\rangle) \rangle\!\rangle, \qquad \xi \in \mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R}),$$
where $\langle\!\langle\cdot,\cdot\rangle\!\rangle$ is the dual pairing. A functional $\Phi \in (\mathcal{S})^*$ is uniquely determined by $T\Phi$, and the characterization theorem states that $F:\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R})\to\mathbb{C}$ equals $T\Phi$ for some $\Phi \in (\mathcal{S})^*$ if and only if $F$ is ray-entire of second order growth and locally uniformly bounded on $\mathcal{S}(\mathbb{R})$.

In the white-noise formulation of quantum mechanics, for suitable potentials $V$ and times $0<t_0<t$, the Feynman integrand for a particle moving from $x_0$ to $x$ in $\mathbb{R}^d$ is formally
$$ I_V \;=\; N \exp\!\Big(\tfrac{i+1}{2}\!\int_{t_0}^{t}\!\!\dot{B}(s)^2\, ds\Big)\,\exp\!\Big(-i\!\int_{t_0}^{t} V(B(s)+x)\, ds\Big)\,\delta(B(t)+x-x_0),$$
and one seeks to realize $I_V$ as an element of $(\mathcal{S})^*$ by verifying that a candidate T-transform $T I_V(\xi)$ exists and satisfies the characterization theorem. In the standard non-perturbative construction (e.g.\ via a Doss-type formula), this verification proceeds by demonstrating integrability of an associated expectation expression that defines $T I_V(\xi)$.

Problem. Determine whether the class of potentials $V$ for which $I_V$ can be rigorously constructed as a generalized white noise functional in $(\mathcal{S})^*$ in a non-perturbative manner can be enlarged by replacing the current pointwise/absolute integrability requirement on the integrand defining the candidate T-transform with a strictly weaker condition (for example, a conditional or oscillatory-integral notion, an analytic continuation, or a distributional limit), in such a way that the resulting $\xi \mapsto T I_V(\xi)$ still satisfies the white-noise characterization theorem and hence defines a unique element of $(\mathcal{S})^*$ whose generalized expectation provides the Green's function of the corresponding Schrödinger equation. Identify explicitly such a weakened integrability condition and the resulting larger class of admissible potentials, or prove that no such weakening is possible while preserving a valid T-transform.
artifact.category_tag: White noise analysis and Feynman path integrals
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature on white-noise Feynman integrals (including work on phase-space and QFT extensions through 2024–2025) continues to construct non-perturbative Feynman integrands under explicit integrability hypotheses on the relevant expectation (e.g. via Doss-type formulas, finite signed measures of bounded support, and Laplace-transformable potentials). No source located states that the integrability requirement has been replaced by a strictly weaker general condition extending the admissible class of potentials. The problem therefore appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Feynman integral in QFT and white noise
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs Feynman integrands as white noise distributions under explicit integrability/characterization hypotheses on the T-transform.
status_evidence.claim: Recent (2024) constructions still rely on integrability of the expression defining the T-transform.

status_evidence.title: Feynman integrals as Hida distributions: the case of non-perturbative potentials
status_evidence.snippet: Non-perturbative construction via Doss formula combined with white noise techniques, requiring integrability conditions on potentials.
status_evidence.claim: Non-perturbative class is delineated by integrability requirements not yet weakened in the literature.

status_evidence.title: White Noise Approach to Feynman Path Integrals and Some of the Related Topics
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of white-noise Feynman integrals describing integrability assumptions used in the construction.
status_evidence.claim: Surveys list integrability as the standing assumption for the construction.
